expected_return.window: scorebord: BUY 13:30 ET on the entry day; SELL amc at the next open, bmo at 13:00 ET on the report day; gross

note: Each member is reported as a percentile of its own live range, 0-100 (pct), with its direction in side; panel_pct (0-100) is the size of the mean of the signed percentiles and side its direction; panel_pct_sd their spread. The selection is panel_pct in the top 20%. panel_score is the signed median of the members' sizes, each read against its own recent history. consensus_k counts members that put the name in their own top 20% on the panel's side; that, not sign agreement, is what selected well on the development names. Certainty (p_up) is recorded and decides nothing. expected_edge_pct is a shrunk in-sample prior, not a forecast. Research only.

opus5.note: Modest negative: the well-linked peer QFIN's Q3 collapse and guide cut (i0) plus the funding-partner/regulatory squeeze (i5) and the lapsing buyback into a $0.5m/day tape (i4) point to a bad quarter, but the expectations item (i1) is decisive on size - the US$6.03 bid pins the price, the stock moved +0.4% on the day QFIN fell 7.6% and did not mark the sector's 15-20% drawdown, so the quarter only matters through the lower-bid channel; no consensus bar exists, which caps every size.

opus55.note: The US$6.03 controller bid (94% of votes) pins XYF and post-proposal prints moved about 1%; the linked QFIN Q3 deterioration and deposit write-down risk lean slightly negative, while a wide 15% spread leaves room for deal-progress language, so this is a small negative lean on an unsourced bar.

sonnet55.note: Stock is pinned by the US$6.03 take-private bid and ignored QFIN's weak print, so only a small negative lean from the linked peer item (QFIN credit erosion, 14.9% offer spread, no guide, cautious tone) survives; the release date is also not company-confirmed in the pack.

fable51.note: Rests on the linked peer QFIN print (item 0, same regulation and funding pool, Q4 guided down 67-77%) and the sector funding squeeze (item 5) pointing to a weak Q3 that could give the 94%-vote buyer cover to trim the US$6.03 bid; sized small because the bid pins the tape (item 1: XYF ignored QFIN's -7.6%), the bar is unsourced, there is no guide, and deal-progress language is the one upside the release could add; items 9-16 dropped as immaterial, outside the window, duplicate or contradicted.
